question: On Bank of America's second-quarter 2026 earnings call (July 14, 2026), what full-year 2026 outlook did the CFO give for (a) net interest income (NII) growth and (b) operating leverage, and how did each compare with the outlook he said had been given earlier in 2026 (in January and/or April)?
grading: Key points (all required): (1) full-year 2026 NII growth expected at the UPPER END of the 6%-8% range (not a new numeric range); (2) full-year 2026 operating leverage expected in the range of 300 to 400 basis points; (3) comparison with earlier outlook: NII growth was 5%-7% in January and raised to 6%-8% in April; operating leverage was 'more than 200 basis points' as of the April (Q1) call. Accept equivalent wording ('top end of 6-8%', '3-4 percentage points'). Fail if the answer gives plain 6%-8% or 5%-7% as the current NII view without 'upper end', gives 'more than 200 bps' as the current operating-leverage view, states a dollar NII figure as guidance, or relies on remarks from the Q3 2026 call (mid-October 2026, after the as_of date) or the mid-September Barclays conference.
answer: (a) Full-year 2026 NII growth is now expected at the upper end of the 6%-8% range (the CFO recalled 5%-7% in January, raised to 6%-8% in April) [W01-E1]. (b) Full-year 2026 operating leverage is now expected to be 300 to 400 basis points, up from 'more than 200 basis points' given on the April call; first-half 2026 operating leverage had already exceeded 450 bps (Q2: 6.6%) [W01-E1]. Neither full-year outlook appears in the July 14 press release or in the slide deck filed with the 8-K [W01-E2, W01-E3].

*As of 2026-10-03*

**Interpreted as:** 'Second-quarter 2026 earnings call (July 14, 2026)' read as the Q2 FY2026 (2026-04-01 to 2026-06-30) earnings call; BAC's fiscal year is the calendar year. 'Full-year 2026 outlook' read as FY2026 (2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31) guidance, which is forward-looking and not yet reported. 'Earlier in 2026 (January and/or April)' read as the FY2026 outlook given at the Q4 FY2025 earnings call (January 2026) and the Q1 FY2026 earnings call (April 2026); the January call's release falls outside the provided FY2026 calendar, so it is covered via the call-coverage search. Guidance figures are taken as the CFO's own statements on the call, not as analyst estimates or our own forecast.

- At Bank of America's Q4 FY2025 earnings call on January 14, 2026, CFO Alastair Borthwick guided to full-year 2026 (calendar year 2026) net interest income on an FTE basis (non-GAAP) growing 5% to 7% versus 2025. [1][2]
- At that same January 14, 2026 call, the CFO guided to about 200 basis points of operating leverage for 2026. [2][3]
- At Bank of America's Q1 FY2026 earnings call on April 15, 2026, the full-year 2026 NII growth outlook was revised upward to a range of 6% to 8% versus 2025, assuming moderate loan and deposit growth. [4]
- Hudson Labs, a secondary source, reported that Bank of America's FY2026 NII growth guidance stood at the top end of a 6–8% range (versus 5–7% at the start of the year) and that FY2026 operating leverage guidance had been raised to 300–400 bps from 200–300 bps previously. [5]
- The Q2 FY2026 earnings release and presentation filed July 14, 2026 (quarter ended June 30, 2026) contain no full-year 2026 NII growth or operating leverage guidance, reporting only quarterly results such as NII of $16.0 billion (GAAP) / $16.2 billion (FTE, non-GAAP), up 9% year-over-year, and operating leverage of 6.6% for the quarter. [6][7]

**Not available**
- CFO's full-year 2026 NII growth outlook as given on the Q2 FY2026 earnings call (July 14, 2026): No transcript, release or presentation of the July 14, 2026 Q2 FY2026 earnings call is included in the provided evidence; the Q2 FY2026 8-K exhibits (EX-99.1, EX-99.2, EX-99.3) contain only quarterly results and interest-rate sensitivity, with no FY2026 NII guidance. [6][7][8]
- CFO's full-year 2026 operating leverage outlook as given on the Q2 FY2026 earnings call (July 14, 2026): The July 14, 2026 call is not covered by any provided evidence; the Q2 FY2026 release and presentation disclose only the 6.6% quarterly operating leverage actual, not FY2026 guidance. [6][7]
- Full-year 2026 operating leverage guidance as given at the Q1 FY2026 earnings call (April 15, 2026): The Q1 FY2026 call transcript excerpt in the evidence gives the revised NII range but no FY2026 operating leverage guidance figure; only the 290 bps Q1 actual is cited. [4]
